editorNote: Alphabet and Rocket Lab both get resolution today: a federal judge preserved Google's ad-tech business by rejecting the DOJ's divestiture demand, while Rocket Lab notched its 94th Electron launch even as its CFO disclosed a routine, plan-based share sale. Bitcoin held near $80,000 on steady corporate buying and a looming Senate vote on crypto market rules, while gold pulled back after a stronger-than-expected jobs report lifted the odds of a near-term Fed rate move.

stories.headline: Judge rejects DOJ's bid to force Google to sell its ad exchange
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema denied the Justice Department's request that Google divest its AdX ad exchange and open-source the final auction logic of its DFP ad server, ruling on September 2 that the structural proposals "be and are REJECTED." She instead accepted most of the parties' proposed behavioral remedies, as modified by the court; the full reasoning stays sealed for 14 days while both sides request redactions, and a joint final judgment is due within 30 days.
stories.whyItMatters: Alphabet keeps its ad-tech business intact rather than facing what commentators called the most consequential structural antitrust breakup of a tech company since the Microsoft case, though Google has signaled it will still appeal the underlying liability finding.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab snaps 3-day slide after 94th Electron launch as CFO sells $8.8M in shares
stories.summary: Rocket Lab completed its 94th Electron mission, "Owl Around The World," from Mahia, New Zealand, deploying Synspective's StriX radar-imaging satellite into a 575km low-Earth orbit after two weather delays; it was the company's 15th launch of 2026 and extends a perfect track record with Synspective, which has 16 more Electron missions booked through 2030. Shares rose 1% to $63.10, snapping a three-session slide, the same day a filing showed CFO Adam Spice plans to sell 140,157 shares (about $8.77 million) acquired via option exercise under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted June 3.
stories.whyItMatters: The launch keeps Rocket Lab's delivery record intact ahead of a large contracted backlog, while the CFO's pre-scheduled, plan-based sale gives investors a concrete data point on insider activity to weigh against it.

stories.headline: Bitcoin holds near $80,000 as corporate buying and a Senate crypto bill stay in focus
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $79,980 on September 6, up 0.43% and still down about 9% year-to-date after rebounding from roughly $63,000 in August. MicroStrategy raised $602.8 million through stock sales between August 24-30 and used $369.7 million of it to buy 4,603 more bitcoin, lifting its total holdings to 845,050 BTC, while the Senate's CLARITY Act, which would split digital-asset oversight between the CFTC and SEC, faces a cloture vote on September 15.
stories.whyItMatters: Continued corporate accumulation and a concrete date for a Senate procedural vote give holders two tangible catalysts to track, rather than pure price speculation.

stories.headline: Gold slips as a stronger-than-expected jobs report lifts Fed rate-hike odds
stories.summary: Gold fell about 0.8% on September 4 to trade near $4,437 after dropping more than 2% intraday, as August nonfarm payrolls came in far above forecast (162,000 versus 56,000 expected). The data pushed money-market odds of a Fed rate increase at the September meeting to 61%, up from 54% a day earlier, and strengthened the dollar, which pressures dollar-priced gold.
stories.whyItMatters: A stronger labor market reshuffles the rate expectations investors use to price gold, with next week's PPI and CPI releases set to test whether the pullback holds.
